questions.q: How many OneLakes exist per Fabric tenant?
options: Exactly one — you can't create a second one
One per workspace
One per Lakehouse
As many as you want, with no real limit
questions.explain: There's exactly one OneLake per tenant, included automatically, with no infrastructure to provision — often described as "OneDrive for data."

questions.q: What makes the "one copy of data, many engines" claim technically possible?
options: OneLake stores data in open formats like Delta Parquet, which any compatible engine can read directly
Microsoft builds a custom connector for every single tool that needs access
Every engine actually gets its own separate copy behind the scenes
It's only true for Power BI, not for Spark or T-SQL
questions.explain: Because OneLake stores tables in open, standard formats like Delta Parquet, Spark, T-SQL, and Power BI's Direct Lake mode can all read the exact same physical data without separate exports or copies.

options: A reference to data stored elsewhere, made to behave as if it were stored locally in OneLake
A keyboard shortcut for common OneLake operations
A compressed copy of data used for faster access
A type of Fabric pipeline activity that only runs once
questions.explain: A shortcut points at data in another workspace, another OneLake item, or an external source, making it look and behave as if it's stored locally — without duplicating it.

questions.q: Why might you use a shortcut instead of a Copy activity to bring another team's data into your workspace?
options: The shortcut reflects source updates immediately, with no scheduled refresh pipeline required
Shortcuts are always faster than Copy activities in every scenario
Copy activities can't move data between Fabric workspaces at all
Shortcuts and Copy activities do exactly the same thing with no differences
questions.explain: A shortcut avoids duplicating the data entirely — when the source updates, the shortcut reflects it immediately, unlike a copied dataset that needs its own refresh pipeline.

questions.q: When a Dataflow Gen2's destination is set to Lakehouse Tables, what actually happens?
options: It writes directly into OneLake, instantly available to other Fabric workloads with no extra data movement
It creates a separate, isolated copy only that Dataflow Gen2 can access
It requires a manual export step before other tools can read the data
It converts the data into a proprietary format only Dataflow Gen2 understands
questions.explain: Writing to Lakehouse Tables means writing directly into OneLake — the same physical data other Fabric experiences in that workspace can read immediately, with zero additional movement.
